routes.serves: note list JSON that feeds the home page notes area (pinned notes and regular notes)
create a note from the Take a note editor (title + content); returns 201 with the created note, 400 on invalid JSON body
update an existing note's title/content/color/labels/reminder; returns 200 with the updated note, 404 when the note does not exist, 400 on invalid JSON body
soft-delete a note (moves it to the Trash); returns 200 with the note, 404 when missing
restore a deleted note from the Trash; returns 200 with the note, 404 when missing
archive or unarchive a note; returns 200 with the updated note, 404 when the note does not exist
pin or unpin a note (defaults to pinned: true; body may carry pinned: false to unpin); returns 200 with the updated note, 404 when the note does not exist
permanently delete a note from the Trash view; returns 200 with the note, 404 when missing
empty the trash; returns 200 with the removed count

notes: REQ-2.8.2 (Unpin note) builds directly on the pin flow from REQ-2.8.1. The backend route POST /api/notes/:id/pin already accepts a body with pinned: false to clear the pinned state (404 on unknown id), and render() already moves an unpinned note from the 'Pinned' section back into the 'Others' section. Two pieces were missing: (1) the note card's Unpin button (aria-label 'Unpin', shown on hover for pinned notes) posted to /api/notes/:id/pin WITHOUT a body, so the backend defaulted to pinned: true and re-pinned the note instead of unpinning it - the handler now sends {pinned: false} when the note is pinned, keeping the plain POST (no body) for the Pin action; (2) the requirement states the system contains a regular (not pinned) note titled 'Meeting agenda 2.8.2', which was not seeded - a seed row (pinned: false, not archived, not deleted) is added to backend/data/db.json so it is reproduced on every fresh start. The acceptance scenario (hover the note, click Pin, then hover again and click Unpin, then see the note back under 'Others') works with the home page's existing Pinned/Others sections. The seed row and the single-line handler fix are additive and do not alter any route, page structure, or existing seed data, so all previously implemented requirements remain unaffected.
